findings.source_passage: For one, I cannot bawl very heartily and work very recklessly at one and the same time.
findings.source_locator: paragraph 1, after 'none know but those who have tried it'
findings.why_it_matters: This self-deprecating first-person aside is a key voice-establishing moment—Ishmael's wry personal confession anchoring the abstract argument in lived experience. Its absence removes the narrator's presence from the passage entirely.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore verbatim: 'For one, I cannot bawl very heartily and work very recklessly at one and the same time.' It is brief and should fit within budget.

findings.source_passage: Now, I care not who maintains the contrary, but all this is both foolish and unnecessary.
findings.why_it_matters: The combative 'I care not who maintains the contrary' is a signature rhetorical gesture establishing Ishmael as opinionated reformer-narrator. The draft collapses it to a bare declarative ('This is foolish and unnecessary'), erasing the defiant voice.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the opening clause: 'Now, I care not who maintains the contrary, but all this is both foolish and unnecessary.'

findings.source_passage: no wonder that to many ship owners, whaling is but a losing concern
findings.source_locator: paragraph 1, in the 'no wonder' anaphora chain
findings.why_it_matters: The 'no wonder' chain builds rhetorically through six items; omitting the 'ship owners' link shortens the cumulative effect and loses a thematic touch connecting individual exhaustion to commercial failure.
findings.suggested_fix: Add 'no wonder that to many ship owners, whaling is but a losing concern' back into the chain.

summary: Two medium-severity voice-flattening losses (the personal aside 'For one, I cannot bawl…' and the combative opener 'I care not who maintains the contrary') weaken Ishmael's narrator presence but do not individually or collectively reach the regeneration threshold; the closing aphorism and core argument survive intact.
